outcome: mean heart rate between 60 to 120 seconds after birth
cohort: 508 infants born at ≥32+0 weeks gestation requiring a paediatrician at birth in 2 Australian perinatal centres.
finding: There was no significant difference in mean heart rate between 60 to 120 seconds after birth for infants receiving physiologically based cord clamping compared to those receiving early cord clamping.
